newsitem.title: BULGARIA: ADTRANZ SIGNS BULGARIAN RAILWAY DEAL.
newsitem.headline: ADTRANZ SIGNS BULGARIAN RAILWAY DEAL.

text.p: European rail technology firm Adtranz and Hungarian Railways' MAV Dunakeszi Wagon Manufacturing and Repairing Ltd (DVJ) on Wednesday signed a $23.8 million contract with Bulgarian State Railways (BSR).

Adtranz, a joint venture between Daimler-Benz of Germany and Swiss/Swedish ABB, and DVJ will provide plant, equipment, components and a project management for the refurbishment of 50 passenger wagons, a statement said.
The consortium will also supply spare parts for the refurbishment of another 50 passenger wagons, it added.

Under the project, financed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Adtranz will supply a railway workshop at the town of Dryanovo in central Bulgaria with modern equipment to enable the refurbishment.
The refurbishment will be carried out by the DVJ through transfer of know-how, project management and material supplies worth $18.9 million, the statement said.
The first refurbished wagons will be delivered to the BSR after a year and the contract will be completed after 28 months.
The wagons, which are a mix of first and second class saloon vehicles supplied by the former East Germany from 1968 to 1972, will be in operation for 20 years after the upgrading.

BSR director general Angel Dimitrov said the firm would invite tenders for a total of 36 projects following last January's parliament ratifications of $170 million credits mainly from the World Bank and the EBRD towards a railway restructuring programme, which totals $296 million.
The railways plan to sign on Thursday the establishment of a joint venture between a Sofia plant for railway points and Austria's VAE Eisenbahnsysteme AG , Dimitrov told a news conference.

Another joint venture has been set up between Italy's Eurofer Ltd and a plant producing sleepers for railway tracks and electric pylons in the Danube river port of Svistov. The plant is expected to start new production at the end of May.

Dimitrov said around December 20 the company would finalise its work for the electrification of a railway stretch from the town of Voluyak, some 15 km (9.4 miles) west of Sofia to the check point of Dragoman on the border with Serbia.
